instructionPdfs.provenance: Archival scan hosted by Rock Raiders United; the pages themselves carry LEGO branding, set number 1277, product code 4132646 and a 1999 LEGO Group copyright notice, but the PDF is not served from LEGO's current archive.

constructionRanges.evidence: Complete flat base, paired yellow side wedges, teal side/rear fittings, central hazard panel and exposed Sparks operator are assembled.
Two raised round side hover/engine pods and two forward ice-saw arms attach to the low open craft; the final model is shown from the front-left three-quarter view.

viewCoverage.mechanism: PARTIAL p2 saw and side-pod attachment; no spin, hover or steering sequence

findings: The complete source is a very low open hovercraft/sled with an exposed operator, not a wheeled miniature drill vehicle.
Two forward ice saws are separate mirrored tool arms; the source does not contain one central helical drill.
Two raised round side pods and the central hazard panel carry more source identity than any rear bodywork.
openGaps: The opposite side and strict underside remain unverified.

The canonical single oversized mining drill is a gameplay adaptation of the paired source saw package; its support must preserve the verified low sled and paired side-pod relationship rather than inventing a wheel chassis.

constructionRanges.evidence: Complete Hover Scout build from flat base plate through open operator deck, front scanner/tool mass and rear equipment.
Separate small worksite/scanner station; useful for the Cutter Mast base language, not a reverse view of the Scout.

viewCoverage.mechanism: PARTIAL p1 scanner/tool mounting; no authored movement sequence

findings: The Scout is an exposed plate-built sled rather than a closed hovercraft.
The operator, scanner/tool and rear rack are independent readable masses.
The second-page station provides a source-faithful tripod/pedestal vocabulary for later survey-derived infrastructure.
openGaps: Acquire explicit underside and opposite-side evidence before final modeling.
Any animated scanner sweep is an approved presentation interpretation, not proven by the manual.

constructionRanges.evidence: Complete twin-hull Rapid Rider build, central deck, raised canopy/bridge, rear drive equipment and carried rock load.

viewCoverage.front: PARTIAL p1 cover and p2 final
viewCoverage.threeQuarter: VERIFIED p1 cover and p2 final
viewCoverage.undersideInterior: PARTIAL p1 steps 1-4 expose hull foundations
viewCoverage.mechanism: PARTIAL p2 rear propulsion and cargo placement; no movement sequence

findings: Two long parallel hulls remain separate around a narrow central deck.
The open load/passenger zone is structural negative space and must not be roofed over.
Rear propulsion and carried cargo are visually subordinate to the twin-hull plan.
openGaps: Acquire a clean orthogonal rear view before final propulsion placement.
Amphibious hover behavior is canonical adaptation and is not demonstrated by the static manual.

viewCoverage.front: VERIFIED archival box and out-of-box photos
viewCoverage.threeQuarter: VERIFIED archival box and out-of-box photos
viewCoverage.mechanism: PARTIAL loose handheld tools and equipment stand; no authored action sequence

findings: The set contains the five named crew minifigures Axle, Bandit, Docs, Jet and Sparks; the figures, not a vehicle, are its primary playable identity.
The remaining source material is a very small equipment/control stand, loose tools including a large handheld saw assembly, and a boulder containing an energy crystal.
4930 provides crew appearance and portable-equipment variation. It does not justify a crew vehicle, a large building or one fixed backpack shared by all five characters.
openGaps: Rear printing and exact backpack/lamp combinations for all five characters remain incomplete in the located product photos; production must use other verified crew appearances or present the variant choice to the game director.

constructionRanges.evidence: Two mirrored ski-foot/leg modules and their shared upper bridge are assembled independently.
Long central drill craft body, cockpit cage, rear wheel/tool mass and drill boom are built as a separate module.
Upper drill module is mounted across the paired leg modules; final operator-scale three-quarter view.

viewCoverage.mechanism: PARTIAL p23 module connection; gait and drill motion not demonstrated

findings: The recognizable walker is a bridge between two mirrored planted foot modules, not a wheeled chassis with decorative legs.
The drill/cockpit body is a removable longitudinal module carried above the feet.
The long drill is structurally balanced by rear wheel/equipment mass and a high open cage.
openGaps: The manual proves modular construction but not a walking gait; leg articulation and contact phases remain an explicit adaptation decision.

constructionRanges.evidence: Wide low chassis, rear frame, control station and paired structural side rails.
Full-width bucket, front linkage, high cage, lighting and wheel mounts.
Explicit bucket lift/tilt play feature and rock-loading pose.

findings: The bucket is carried by visible side linkages and must remain the dominant forward mass.
Four equal large wheels sit outside a broad plate-built chassis.
The operator cage is rear-weighted, leaving the front linkage and bucket visually exposed.
openGaps: Opposite-side product photography is still desirable for exact hose and control placement.

constructionRanges.evidence: Long forked chassis and independently built front control side modules.
Motor block, raised frame, cockpit cage, cargo deck and flexible power/tool routing.
Overhead tool/light beam, drill subassembly, wheel/light modules and final machine assembly.
Drill motor operation/safety evidence and final mechanism instructions.

viewCoverage.undersideInterior: VERIFIED p2-20 chassis and motor build
viewCoverage.mechanism: VERIFIED p27-36 drill drive, wheel modules and movable tool/light assembly

findings: The vehicle is a long open industrial chassis wrapped around motor, cargo and tool systems rather than a solid armored hull.
The powered drill projects far beyond the front cage and is mechanically connected to the internal motor.
Four huge wheels are separate side modules; the raised work-light/tool beam forms a second skyline above the drill.
openGaps: A strict orthogonal rear photograph remains desirable for final cargo and cable clearance.

constructionRanges.evidence: Forward cockpit/cargo vehicle module with low worksite chassis and open load bed.
Separate compact wheeled support module.
Wide rotor transport frame, twin propeller pods and attachment to the carried modules.
Cargo container, alternate carried load and final multi-angle product photography.

viewCoverage.undersideInterior: VERIFIED p21-29 open transport frame and load connections
viewCoverage.mechanism: PARTIAL p21-29 rotors and cargo attachment; no rotor animation sequence

findings: The aircraft is a skeletal load-bearing bridge with two giant rotor pods, not a conventional enclosed helicopter fuselage.
Carried modules remain visibly independent beneath/within the transport frame.
The long crossbeam, pod spacing and open central cradle are the primary structural identity.
openGaps: Rotor pitch and suspension response are not authored by the manual and remain presentation interpretations.

constructionRanges.evidence: Small work vehicles, crystal handling and compact workstation modules.
Tall illuminated machinery/power tower with open service access.
Long articulated crane/tool boom mounted to the tower and used for rock handling.
Open vehicle-width gantry/workshop with sloped supports, lamps and overhead rails.
Conveyor/processing module attaches to the gantry and completes a visible material route.
Modules connect across an irregular rock worksite base rather than a sealed building shell.
Final product photography supplies overall skyline, module spacing and worksite context.

viewCoverage.undersideInterior: VERIFIED p2-40 staged module and base construction
viewCoverage.mechanism: VERIFIED p11-19 crane/tool boom; PARTIAL p20-34 gantry/conveyor service path

findings: HQ identity comes from a loose network of independently readable work modules on an uneven base, not from a single enclosed headquarters block.
Tower, articulated crane, open vehicle gantry and conveyor/processing path establish the reusable infrastructure grammar.
Entrances and service lanes remain physically open and minifigure/vehicle scaled.
openGaps: The manual supports modular industrial functions but does not assign the game's exact Ore Plant, Power Station, Service Bay or Workshop boundaries; those remain explicit canonical adaptations.
